confidence_explanation: The timeline shows a clear progression from external SQL injection attempts to a successful account takeover/compromise of user_07, followed by privilege escalation, massive data exfiltration via DNS tunneling and HTTPS, and finally log tampering to hide tracks.

attack_chain.description: External attacker (104.244.76.13) performs SQL injection attempts against the web server using sqlmap.
Attacker successfully logs into user_07's account from the same malicious IP (104.244.76.13) during off-hours.
The compromised account (user_07) performs privilege escalation, elevating their role to 'dba'.
The attacker uses the elevated privileges to run large queries against the 'prod_main' database, targeting the 'customers' table.
Data exfiltration begins via DNS tunneling to a known malicious domain (x4798.malicious-53.com).
Massive data exfiltration continues via HTTPS (port 443), transferring hundreds of megabytes of data.
The attacker attempts to cover their tracks by deleting the authentication logs (/var/log/auth.log).

gaps: Confirmation of whether the SQL injection (evt_s97_001-005) was the direct mechanism used to obtain user_07's credentials.
Identification of the specific destination for the HTTPS exfiltration.
narrative: An attacker used SQL injection attempts to facilitate the compromise of user_07's account. Once inside, the attacker escalated privileges to DBA, queried large volumes of customer data, exfiltrated approximately 290MB of data via DNS and HTTPS, and finally deleted authentication logs to evade detection.
